sources.section: Env Variables and Modes > Env Variables

tasks.answer: Only variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to client code via `import.meta.env`; the prefix is changed with the `envPrefix` option (string or string[], default `VITE_`, must not be `''`).

Configure `server.proxy` in vite.config, e.g. `'/api': { target: 'http://backend', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (path) => path.replace(/^\/api/, '') }` (or the string shorthand `'/api': 'http://host'`); requests whose path starts with the key are forwarded to the target.

Use library mode via the `build.lib` option (`entry`, `name`, `fileName`, optional `formats`, default `['es','umd']`) and externalize dependencies you do not want bundled with `build.rolldownOptions.external` (plus `output.globals` for UMD).

sources.section: Deploying a Static Site > GitHub Pages

tasks.answer: Set `base` to `'/<REPO>/'` in vite.config.js when deploying to `https://<USERNAME>.github.io/<REPO>/`, then set Settings > Pages > Source to GitHub Actions and add a `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` workflow that builds and deploys.

sources.section: Dependency Pre-Bundling > Caching > File System Cache

tasks.answer: Start the dev server with the `--force` flag, or delete the `node_modules/.vite` cache directory (the config equivalent is `optimizeDeps.force: true`).
tasks.note: The config option is documented separately in docs/config/dep-optimization-options.md, 'Dependency Optimization Options > optimizeDeps.force' (lines 71-76); the CLI flag also appears in docs/guide/cli.md `vite` options table (line 24).

tasks.answer: Call `import.meta.hot.accept((newModule) => { ... })` (written exactly as `import.meta.hot.accept(` for Vite's static analysis) inside an `if (import.meta.hot) { ... }` block, because the guard lets the HMR code be tree-shaken out of the production build.

Avoid barrel files (index files that re-export a directory): importing one API from a barrel forces Vite to fetch and transform every file it re-exports, so import the individual module directly, e.g. `import { slash } from './utils/slash.js'`.
tasks.note: The docs frame barrel files as slowing the initial page load (more files fetched and transformed), not server start-up itself.

sources.section: Static Asset Handling > Importing Asset as URL > Importing Asset as String

tasks.answer: Append the `?raw` suffix to the import, e.g. `import shaderString from './shader.glsl?raw'`.

`server.allowedHosts` lists the hostnames the dev server may respond to (a leading `.` allows a domain and all subdomains; `true` allows any host but is unsafe due to DNS rebinding); the `__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` env variable can add more.
Add the dependency to `ssr.noExternal` (string, RegExp or array), which prevents it from being externalized so it is processed and bundled by Vite.

In dev just navigate to the nested `/nested/` path; for build specify each `.html` file as an entry in `input` (e.g. `input: { main: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'index.html'), nested: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'nested/index.html') }`).

sources.section: Building for Production > Load Error Handling

tasks.answer: Listen for the `vite:preloadError` window event (e.g. reload the page, optionally calling `event.preventDefault()` to suppress the throw) and serve the HTML with `Cache-Control: no-cache` so old assets are not referenced.
Set `enforce: 'pre'` on the plugin; user plugins with `enforce: 'pre'` run after Alias but before Vite core plugins.
`build.target` defaults to `'baseline-widely-available'`, i.e. `['chrome111', 'edge111', 'firefox114', 'safari16.4', 'ios16.4']` (Baseline Widely Available as of 2026-01-01 for this major).

sources.section: Configuring Vite > Using Environment Variables in Config

tasks.answer: `.env*` files are not loaded into `process.env` while the config runs; export the config as a function and call `loadEnv(mode, process.cwd(), '')` (third argument `''` loads all variables regardless of the `VITE_` prefix).
Import `createServer` from 'vite', call `const server = await createServer({ ...inline config })`, then `await server.listen()` (and optionally `server.printUrls()`).
The documentation does not describe a `server.compressResponses` option.
